title: slice-activation-sla-playbook-scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for defining an SLA-driven slice activation protocol. Goal: make it explicit when and how to open additional traffic slices for a rollout based on production SLAs (latency, errors, quality), cost thresholds, and human approvals. This doc intentionally mixes checklists, raw ideas, and questions to iterate quickly before formalizing into the rollout playbook.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to new LLM feature rollouts and model swaps that use progressive exposure (canaries -> expansion waves -> full).
- ‘Slice’ = cohort of users or traffic path where a variant is active (by region, customer tier, route, or random cohort).
- We assume instrumentation is available: token latency p50/p95/p99, request error rate (5xx), model-quality signals (eval-run pass rate, hallucination proxy), cost per 1k tokens, and user-level degradation metrics (CTR, task completion).
- This is not the final runbook; it focuses on activation gating and emergency degradation decisions.

Key principles (working):
1) SLA-first gating: only activate slices when current and candidate variant meet explicit SLA criteria for at least two consecutive sampling windows.
2) Multi-signal validation: require agreement across latency, availability, and a quality proxy (e.g., hallucination score or eval-based metric).
3) Fast rollback path: every activation must include an automated rollback trigger and a named contact for manual revoke.
4) Cost-aware expansion: don't exceed monthly cost budget cadence for Dedicated customers; include soft cost thresholds that pause progression.
5) Human-in-the-loop for high-risk slices: regulatory or enterprise cohorts require product + security + customer-success signoff.

Activation thresholds (draft numbers — needs empirical tuning):
- Latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.25 and p99 <= baseline_p99 * 1.5
- Error rate (5xx + inference errors): <= baseline_error_rate + 0.2 percentage points (absolute) OR relative increase <= 20%
- Model-quality proxy (eval pass rate on seed prompt set): delta >= -1.0 percentage points vs baseline
- Cost: projected incremental cost for next 7 days <= cost_budget_slice
- Observability coverage: tracing + token-level cost breakdown + per-request IDs available for the slice

Activation ceremony (quick checklist for moving from N% -> N+1%):
- Owner picks activation window and communicates on #release-rollouts channel (who, what, when).
- Confirm telemetry: dashboards populated, alerting rules indexed for the slice.
- Run pre-activation sanity: smoke test set (10–20 synthetic requests) through variant; sample outputs captured.
- Verify telemetry warmup: baseline metrics stable for 30m, candidate warmup at small traffic (0.5% or synthetic) for 15m.
- Approve expansion in ticket with timeboxed observation window (recommended 1 hour at early stages).
- Toggle traffic change and annotate rollout log with timestamp, slice id, change owner.
- Post-activation: accelerate follow-up checks at 5m/15m/60m and record pass/fail.

Automated gating algorithm (sketch):
Inputs: current_metrics, candidate_metrics, baseline (pre-rollout), config thresholds
Steps:
- Aggregate metrics over two rolling windows: short (5m) and medium (30m).
- For each metric type, compute z = (candidate - baseline) / baseline (for rates) or absolute delta (for small percentages).
- Vote rule: metric votes pass if within threshold. Need >=2/3 vote across (latency, error, quality, cost, availability) to allow activation.
- Safety overrides: if any metric breaches 'fatal' limit (e.g., p99 > baseline * 2 or error_rate > baseline + 1 percentage point), block and auto-rollback.

Emergency degradation matrix (draft):
Severity levels and actions:
- Sev-1 (user-facing regression, high volume): immediate traffic rollback to previous variant; page oncall SRE + product; open incident in incident tracker; freeze further activations.
- Sev-2 (degraded quality but limited impact): pause expansion and reduce traffic by 50%; alert oncall; run targeted sampling.
- Sev-3 (observability gaps or minor latency blips): hold expansion, increase sampling and monitoring cadence.

Roles & responsibilities (practical):
- Release owner (usually product PM): decides activation windows, documents hypothesis, writes ticket.
- Release steward (platform engineer / release engineer): implements traffic config, runway, annotates rollout console, ensures rollout can be toggled programmatically.
- Oncall SRE: owns rollback automation and ensures infra-level fallbacks (e.g., fallback to smaller model or different region).
- Observability lead (SRE/infra/observability): verifies dashboards and sets temporary alert thresholds for window.
- Customer Success (for enterprise slices): approves schedule and coordinates comms if customers see change.

Communication templates (copyable):
- Pre-activation announcement:
  Subject: [Rollout] Activate slice {slice-id} -> {new-variant}, {N}% -> {N+X}% at {time}
  Body: Owner: {name}
  Hypothesis: {short}
  Telemetry: dashboard link, smoke test link
  Stop criteria: list of metrics and thresholds
  Page: {oncall}@redwood.ai

- Post-activation update (5/15/60m):
  Status: OK / Monitoring / Rolled back
  Key metrics: p95/p99 latency, error rate, cost delta, quality proxy delta
  Actions: next steps

Data capture + postmortem triggers:
- Capture a decision-log entry every activation with ticket id, owner, metrics snapshot, artifacts (sample responses), and whether rollback occurred.
- Auto-trigger postmortem when any of: rollback occurred, quality proxy drop > 2 p.p., error rate spike > 0.5 p.p., or cost > budgeted threshold for 24 hours.

Open questions / items to validate:
- Which exact quality proxies are reliable early in rollout? (hallucination detector, safety classifier, user feedback signals?)
- Sampling windows: are 5m/30m sufficient for LLM workloads that may have high variance? Consider 1h/4h for certain signals.
- Cost model: how to predict short-term burst cost vs monthly amortized costs for Dedicated customers.
- Should we always require manual signoff for enterprise slices even if automated gates pass? (probably yes)

Quick experiments to run (next 2 sprints):
1) Backtest thresholds: run historical rollout traces through gate algorithm and surface false positives/negatives. Owner: Evan Zhao. Ticket: ROLL-4310.
2) Evaluate quality proxies: run a 500-prompt seed set across models and measure stability across 1h windows. Owner: Priya Rao.
3) Run cost-sensitivity sim: vary traffic and sequence length distributions to model 7-day cost projections. Owner: Jordan Blake.

Notes to self / shorthand ideas:
- Consider an internal 'safety token' – a temporary lower-rate path that carries weight but limited to low-cost requests for faster signal.
- Could leverage canary model variants with quantized weights to reduce cost while testing semantics.
- Think about making the gating system pluggable so product teams can opt into stricter thresholds for regulated features.

Related artifacts / examples to pull from while formalizing:
- staged-deployment-signal-runbook (use the signal taxonomy)
- canary-post-decision-checklist-and-incident-notifications (for comms)
- commit logs from last three model rollouts (PRODOPS-854, PRODOPS-911)

Immediate next steps to clean up this doc:
- Get feedback from SRE (oncall) about fatal limits and rollback latency requirements.
- Run backtest experiments and iterate thresholds.
- Draft a single-page playbook from this scratchpad to replace current ad-hoc checklist.

End of scratchpad.

(untidy — intentionally; will refine into structured playbook once experiments finish)
